question:
MorphStudio P8b, one item: mcpserver/pm.go (contour.yaml group mcpserver, Function PM Tools) is rewritten from the record by a card that never sees the current file; PMServer gains the tool `events`, UserServer gains `project_adopt`.
Contract: the record's PM Tools behavior (ServerName, ServerVersion, UserServer, PMServer). Unchanged and not rewritten: mcpserver/session.go, mcpserver/mount.go and their tests.
Out of scope: daemon, cmd, control, api.
Question: which identifiers declared in mcpserver/pm.go today (exported or private: funcs, types, consts) are used by mcpserver/session.go, mcpserver/mount.go or any other non-pm file? Give file:line for each use.
Name every test and caller that relies on the old pm.go names.

answer.reasoning: pm.go declares 18 package-scope identifiers: consts ServerName (pm.go:15) and ServerVersion (pm.go:18); type Empty (pm.go:21); funcs jsonResult (pm.go:24), errorResult (pm.go:35), UserServer (pm.go:106), PMServer (pm.go:135); types projectsView (44), okView (49), questionView (54), stopView (59), projectCreateInput (64), orderInput (71), answerInput (76), restartInput (81), planLoadInput (86), planPhaseInput (92), capsInput (99), plus the 10 tool names registered as string literals inside the two constructors. Only five of them are used by a non-pm file, all inside package mcpserver: ServerName and ServerVersion in mcpserver/session.go:59 (SessionServer's mcp.NewServer); errorResult in session.go:66, :79, :96; jsonResult in session.go:68, :81, :98; okView in session.go:68, :81, :98. Across the whole module UserServer is called only at mcpserver/mount.go:39 (the /mcp streamable handler) and PMServer only at mcpserver/mount.go:43 (/mcp/{project}); every other use is in the same directory. Empty, projectsView, questionView, stopView and all nine *Input types are referenced nowhere but pm.go itself (Empty is merely documented in docs/DECISIONS.md:162 and docs/TASK_P6_mcpserver.md:273 as an extra export; docs/deps/go-sdk.md:28-37 only explains the pattern) — so they may be renamed or dropped freely. Callers that rely on the old pm.go names: mcpserver/pm_examples_test.go:238, :253, :269, :306, :336, :421 call PMServer and :392 calls UserServer, and the file's examples pin the old behaviour that the rewrite changes — TestPMToolsExample1 (pm_examples_test.go:234-248) asserts exactly the ten tool names, and TestPMToolsExample6 (pm_examples_test.go:373-414) asserts exactly ["project_create","projects_list"] and a zero-adopt call list, so with PMServer gaining events and UserServer gaining project_adopt this test file must be regenerated by the pm-tools-judge card (morph-map.json:94-95 names mcpserver/pm_examples_test.go as that card's only target) — it is a target, not context. mcpserver/mount_examples_test.go is an indirect caller: it names no pm.go identifier but drives both constructors through mcpserver.Handler and re-asserts the same tool lists at mount_examples_test.go:224 (ten PM tools) and :320 (["project_create","projects_list"]), so it silently re-tests pm.go's tool set; cmd/morphd/main.go:36 is the same kind of indirect caller (mcpserver.Handler / mcpserver.Tokens only). Per the task both mount_examples_test.go and session.go/mount.go are to stay unchanged, so the risk is that the two stale tool-list assertions above must not break the card. Nothing in cmd, api, daemon, control or tests/ references any pm.go name other than through mcpserver.Handler.
